intent.text: I strongly support this motion. It aligns cleanly with the model-family diversity perspective: epistemic diversity is achieved primarily by breaking correlated failure modes across architectures/pre-training sets, which a single cross-family reviewer accomplishes directly. Crucially, condition 1 (verifier sees only the artifact and claims, not author reasoning) protects against cross-family sycophancy/priming, while condition 2 ensures falsifiable claim verification. Reserving councils for normative/trade-off decisions rather than raw verification is the exact right division of labor.
